fields.features_heading: What the Page Behind the Code Needs
fields.features_subheading: A QR code landing page is the web page a printed QR code opens on a phone. These six parts make the scan worth it.
fields.feature_1:
One prompt for each printed piece

Describe the bag or postcard the code goes on and what a scan should do. Emergent builds the page, its form, and the table behind it, and changes it when you prompt again.
fields.feature_2:
Its own link for every placement

Give each table tent, bag, or mail route a link with a tag, such as ?route=a. The page saves that tag with every signup, and your table shows which print brought each person in.
fields.feature_3:
Every entry is a row you own

Every form entry lands as a row in a database you own, with its tag and arrival time. Built apps connect to any tool with an API, so a new row can also update a contact in HubSpot.
fields.feature_4:
An alert when a scan needs a person

Set a rule, such as a visitor asking for a callback today. Each entry that matches sends a Slack message, an email, or an in-app alert to the person who should follow it up.
fields.feature_5:
A live count for each placement

The dashboard behind the page updates live as entries arrive. Split it by tag to compare two posters or two store displays before you pay to print a second run of either one.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain in the code, the code in GitHub

Put your own domain in the printed link; custom domains are included and use credits. On paid plans, the full code exports to your GitHub repository, for a developer to extend.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Pages Behind Printed QR Codes
fields.tab_content_1:
Low ratings reach the manager with the table number

Pickwell Noodle Bar puts a QR code on each of its 18 table tents, and each code carries its table number. The page asks for a rating out of 5 and one comment. Ratings of 2 or below go to manager Odalys Fenwick: when table 14 rated dinner 2 out of 5, she got a Slack message naming table 14.
fields.tab_content_2:
Each refill signup keeps the lot printed on the bag

Copperline Coffee prints a QR code on each bag that opens the brew guide for that roast, with a refill signup below it. Desmond Achterberg scanned a bag from lot 0917 and chose a refill every 3 weeks. His row saved lot 0917 next to his email and the schedule he picked.
fields.tab_content_3:
Two postcard routes, one booking count for each

Halvard Plumbing mailed 4,000 postcards on two mail routes, and each route's card carries its own QR code. Both codes open the same page with $40 off a drain cleaning. The dashboard counts 112 bookings so far: 71 from the north route and 41 from the south route.
fields.tab_content_4:
Thandiwe Morrow gets every lead with 40 trucks or more

At its trade show booth, Ferrovane, which sells fleet tracking, shows a QR code that opens a demo request asking for fleet size. Each lead lands in HubSpot tagged Booth 2214. Fleets of 40 trucks or more also email rep Thandiwe Morrow, and Larchmont Freight entered 65 trucks.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a QR Code Landing Page
fields.howto_description: These seven steps take a QR code landing page from one prompt to a printed code you have tested on real phones.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide where the code will be printed
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Give each printed piece its own link
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Match the headline to the print
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask only for what the next step needs
fields.howto_step_1_des: Picture the spot where the code will hang and how far away people will stand to scan it. A table tent is read at arm's length, while a poster on a far wall is not. Size the printed code for the longest distance you expect.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Add a tag to the link for each placement, such as ?src=tent or ?route=north. That tag is stored on each entry the page receives. Two postcards that share one link can never be told apart once the entries come in.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write a headline that says what the scan gives, in the same words as the printed piece. If the poster promises a free sample, the page should open on the free sample. Keep the headline to one line on a phone screen.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Keep the form to the fields the next step needs: an email for a refill, or a fleet size before a sales call. Every extra field is one more thing to type with a thumb while standing in a store aisle.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste the headline, the form fields, and the tag names into one prompt. Emergent returns a working page you can open on your own phone right away. Any change after that, from a new field to a new headline, is one more prompt.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Publish on a domain people know
fields.howto_step_6_des: Publish the page on a domain your customers already know, and do it before you make the code. Someone deciding whether to open a scanned link should see a name they recognize in it, not a string of random characters.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Make the code from the final link, print one proof, and scan it with two different phones in the light where it will hang. Send a test entry from each phone and check that both rows show the right tag.

faq_plan.q: What is a QR code landing page?
faq_plan.a: A QR code landing page is the page someone reaches by scanning a QR code on a package or a poster. It carries one message that matches the printed piece and one action, such as a short form, sized for a phone screen.

faq_plan.q: How to create a QR landing page?
faq_plan.ref: How to create a QR landing page?

prov.original: How to create a QR landing page?

faq_plan.a: Build the page first, then make the code from its final link. Describe the page and its offer in one prompt to Emergent's AI landing page builder and publish it. Give every printed piece its own tagged link, make a QR code from each, and scan a printed proof before the full run.

faq_plan.q: Where can I create a free landing page for my QR code?
faq_plan.ref: Where can I create a free landing page for my QR code?

prov.original: Where can I create a free landing page for my QR code?

faq_plan.a: You can build and publish one on Emergent for free, since the free tier covers building and publishing. Describe the page and its form in a prompt, publish it, and turn its link into a code with a QR code generator. Each signup is stored in your own database.

faq_plan.q: What are the best practices for a QR code landing page?
faq_plan.ref: qr code landing page best practices
faq_plan.secondary: qr code landing page best practices
faq_plan.a: Treat it as a mobile landing page first, because every visitor arrives from a phone camera. Repeat the printed offer in the headline word for word, ask for one thing, and keep the form on one screen. Under the code on the print, add a short line that says what the scan opens, such as Rate your meal.

faq_plan.q: What are some QR code landing page examples worth copying?
faq_plan.a: Good examples open on the exact thing the person was looking at when they scanned. A yard sign can open the listing with a showing request, and a museum label can open the notes for that one piece. A product manual can open setup steps next to a warranty registration form.

faq_plan.q: Does a QR code landing page generator make the QR code too?
faq_plan.a: Not every one does, so treat the page and the code as two separate jobs. Make the page first, then paste its final link into any QR code generator to make the code itself. If a generator offers to host the page too, ask where your form entries will be stored before you print anything.

faq_plan.q: Should a QR code landing page play a video?
faq_plan.a: Only when the video is what the scan promised, such as setup steps printed on a product box. Keep the clip short and start it muted. Put the button or form above it so a visitor can act without watching. When one clip carries the whole pitch, build a video landing page around it instead.

faq_plan.q: How do I track which flyer or poster a QR landing page scan came from?
faq_plan.a: Give each flyer or poster its own link with a tag, then make a separate QR code from each link. Google's Analytics help says to add utm parameters in order to identify the campaigns that refer traffic. A tag such as utm_source=lobby_poster then marks the visits from that poster. Settle the tag names before anything goes to print.

faq_plan.q: Can I change the landing page for a QR code after it is printed?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as long as the link itself stays the same. A static code has the destination URL placed directly into it, and that URL can't be modified, but the page at that URL can change whenever you edit it. A dynamic code holds a short URL that redirects, and its destination can be changed after the code is created. On Emergent, a change to the page is one more prompt.

faq_plan.q: How long should the form be on a QR code landing page?
faq_plan.a: Keep it to three fields or fewer when the scan leads to a signup or a rating. If the next step needs more, split it into a multi step form with one or two questions per screen. Forms built on Emergent have no response caps.

intent.evidence: Definition in the features subheading and FAQ 1 (AI Overview); four examples by print placement (table tents, packaging, direct mail, booth); 7-step how-to from print placement to tested proof; best practices, examples and generator questions answered.

specificity.evidence: Print-specific detail: 'A table tent is read at arm's length', 'scan it with two different phones in the light where it will hang', per-placement tags '?route=north'. LP table variant.

openers.evidence: Tabs open on a scene ('Pickwell Noodle Bar puts a QR code on each of its 18 table tents'); steps open on an instruction ('Picture the spot where the code will hang').

craft.evidence: QC Q5 at 2 ', so' endings (limit 3); sentences carry one idea each.

truth.evidence: Emergent claims map to prompt-build, database-owned, api-connect (HubSpot), alerts, realtime ('updates live'), custom-domain ('included and use credits'), code-export ('On paid plans'), free-start, no-caps. distinct.evidence: No sibling primary in headings; mobile landing page, video landing page and multi step form appear only as body links in FAQ answers.
